name: Goldspan Dragon
oracle_text:
Flying, haste
Whenever this creature attacks or becomes the target of a spell, create a Treasure token.
Treasures you control have "{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Add two mana of any one color."
blocked_sentences: Whenever this creature attacks or becomes the target of a spell, create a Treasure token.

needs.what: A way for a `becomes_target` trigger to say it fires only on a SPELL -- the natural spelling being a boolean on TriggerSpec (src/automtg/engine/carddef.py:443), e.g. `spell_only: true` (or `by: "spell"`), validated in the loader's trigger builder, added to `trigger_keys`, and compared in `triggers._matches` (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:1029, beside the `filter` check) against the `is_spell` flag that `stack.announce_targets` (src/automtg/engine/stack.py:144-186) ALREADY puts on every BECAME_TARGET event it fires, for both the object and the player half. The event data is there; nothing reads it. One spec field plus one comparison turns on the whole family of printed 'becomes the target of a spell' cards (Goldspan Dragon, heroic, and every 'whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell you control' line), as distinct from the 'spell or ability' family ward already covers.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `becomes_target` is in trigger_events and fires with `source: "self"` exactly as needed -- but it fires for ABILITIES as well as spells, and no key on the trigger can narrow it. Every shipped user of it is ward (Vein Ripper, Grey Host Reinforcements, Coppercoat Vanguard, Lavaspur Boots, Winged Boots), whose printed text is 'a spell or ability an opponent controls', so the unrestricted event is exactly right there and exactly wrong here. `filter` cannot do it: `_matches` hands it to `matches_card_filter` against the trigger's SUBJECT oid, which for `becomes_target` is the permanent being targeted (the Dragon itself, per OBJECT_SUBJECT_TRIGGERS in triggers.py), never the spell doing the targeting -- so it can only ask what the Dragon is. `controller` answers whose spell or ability it was, not what kind. A `condition` cannot reach it either: `event_bindings` copies only EVENT_BINDING_KEYS, which carries `sid` but not `is_spell`, and `was_cast` is asked of the ability's own source (the Dragon) rather than of the targeter. Writing a bare `becomes_target` would make the Dragon mint a Treasure off an opponent's tapper, off a Rabid Bite-style fight ability, or off your own Equip activation -- a strictly larger card, so no partial answer was written. The other near miss, and the reason this is filed rather than worked around: `spell_cast` with `controller: "any"` and an intervening-if of `{"exists": {"binding": "spell_targets", "self_only": true, "zone": "battlefield"}}` (the Orvar, the All-Form shape). It is wrong twice. It misses a COPY of a spell -- a copy is put on the stack, not cast, so it fires BECAME_TARGET but no SPELL_CAST, and `spell_targets` is written by `Game._cast`. And it is an intervening-if, which `stack.resolve_top` re-asks on resolution (603.4, stack.py:1076): kill the Dragon in response and the condition now finds nothing on the battlefield and the Treasure is silently skipped -- which is the exact interaction the printed card exists for.

notes: Only this one sentence is blocked; the rest of the card is expressible today and should not be re-explored. Flying and haste are keywords. The 'attacks' half of the blocked line is an ordinary `attacks` trigger with `source: "self"` and `create_token` of `treasure_token`, and splitting one printed line across two triggered abilities that share the same `text` is an established pattern (99 cards in the shipped pool do it), so the 'or' itself is not the problem -- only the spell restriction on the second half is. The third line is a `grant_ability` static with `affects: {"controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Treasure"]}` pointing at a `grantable_abilities` entry: an `is_mana_ability` activated ability with cost `{"tap": true, "sacrifice": {"self_only": true, ...}}` and a five-mode `choose_mode` whose modes add `{W}{W}` / `{U}{U}` / `{B}{B}` / `{R}{R}` / `{G}{G}` -- `_sum_mana` sums a multi-symbol string, so 'two mana of any one color' needs nothing new. Chromatic Lantern and Paradise Mantle already grant an activated mana ability this way.
